questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: In the 2-D Cartesian coordinate system, what is the specific designation for the point of intersection of the x-axis and y-axis?
questions.explanationAnswer: The point of intersection of the two perpendicular axes (x-axis and y-axis) is defined as the origin $(0, 0)$.
questions.explanationQuestion: This tests the fundamental definition of the coordinate system origin.

questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: If a point $P(x, y)$ has a negative x-coordinate and a positive y-coordinate, in which quadrant does it lie?
questions.explanationAnswer: By convention, Quadrant II is defined by negative x-values and positive y-values $(-, +)$.
questions.explanationQuestion: This tests the knowledge of quadrant sign conventions.

questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: True or False: For any point lying strictly on the x-axis, the y-coordinate must be zero.
questions.explanationAnswer: Since the x-axis is the line where the vertical distance from the origin is zero, all points on it have the form $(x, 0)$.
questions.explanationQuestion: This tests the understanding of axis properties.

questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: True or False: The coordinate pair $(3, 5)$ is identical to the coordinate pair $(5, 3)$ in a 2-D Cartesian plane.
questions.explanationAnswer: In coordinate geometry, the order of elements in the ordered pair $(x, y)$ is significant; therefore, $(3, 5) \neq (5, 3)$.
questions.explanationQuestion: This tests the understanding of ordered pairs.

questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: Given two points $A(3, 4)$ and $D(7, 1)$, calculate the distance $AD$ using the distance formula derived from the Baudhayana-Pythagoras Theorem. Show your steps.

subjective_evaluation_points.point: Identify the distance formula: $d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$

questions.explanationQuestion: This tests the application of the distance formula.

questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: A rectangle has three of its vertices at $(0, 0)$, $(12, 0)$, and $(12, 10)$. Determine the coordinates of the fourth vertex and justify your answer.

subjective_evaluation_points.point: Identify that for a rectangle with sides parallel to the axes, the fourth point must share an x-coordinate with one point and a y-coordinate with another.
Analyze the coordinates: $(0,0)$ to $(12,0)$ is a horizontal base, $(12,0)$ to $(12,10)$ is a vertical side.
State the fourth vertex must be $(0, 10)$ to complete the rectangle.

questions.explanationQuestion: This tests the application of coordinate geometry to identify geometric shapes.
